Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked for a concrete "demand profile" to attach to the PO so they can size the initial reserved fleet and budget for burst windows.

Can you send a template/example showing the following so our infra and procurement teams can sign off:
- steady-state RPS / concurrency per model (we have 3 models in scope)
- expected prompt and response token distributions (p50/p90 lengths)
- hourly burst curves (both expected peak and extreme stress duration)
- failover strategy if Dedicated capacity is saturated (preferred model variants / fallback to hosted)

I can send a traffic snapshot from our prod logs if that helps. Ideally we want numbers by weekday/time-of-day for the first 90 days post-launch.

Hi Aditi, Naomi — looping in a few technical pointers so the worksheet maps cleanly to sizing output.

Summary of assumptions we will use unless you specify otherwise:
- baseline: each NVIDIA A100-80GB (or equivalent) GPU serves approx 18 simultaneous chat-like concurrency slots for 4k context on our optimized runtime for the LLM family you demoed (we'll tune for the exact architecture once we have weights).
- batching profile: steady-state requests use 16–32ms batching windows; bursts increase queue depth and batching efficiency but also increase p99 queueing latency.
- KV cache: interactive chat workstreams with long conversation histories benefit from prefix caching — please indicate average conversation length in messages to estimate KV memory pressure.
- fallback policy: recommended default is to route to (1) lower-precision quantized replica in Dedicated, (2) Hosted overflow if Dedicated pool is fully saturated — we can set a throttling guardrail per-customer.

Clarifying questions for your sheet:
1) Are your 3 models ranked by quality vs cost (e.g., model-A high-quality 2x cost, model-B mid, model-C low)? If yes, indicate % traffic share.
2) For burst windows, do you have absolute expected RPS multipliers or target p99 latency caps (we can map either to required temporary pool growth).
3) Any regulatory constraint on token retention or KV caching? That affects memory vs compute tradeoffs.

Once we have the populated sheet Naomi will schedule a 30-min model-to-deck run with your infra lead and I'll produce a conservative + aggressive capacity plan and an ops runbook for day-1 failover.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
